narrative.synopsis: Hera’s persecution turns Heracles’ strength inward against his own house. When sanity returns, the hero’s guilt drives him to purification and to the labors that will define his life.
narrative.openingSituation: Heracles appears victorious enough to have a family and future.
narrative.centralConflict: A divine attack makes the hero himself the danger to those he loves.
narrative.resolution: Heracles seeks divine instruction and submits to Eurystheus.
narrative.outcome: The Labors become atonement rather than mere adventure.
